topic: Popeyes founder Al Copeland lost the chain in bankruptcy, then used the bankruptcy process itself to force the banks to pay him for the name
title: Popeyes Founder Lost Everything. Then He Made the Banks Pay Him.
note: Gemini first draft, NOT fact-checked. Claude must verify every claim with its own 2-source rule before using any of it in a real job file.
draft_script:
Al Copeland built Popeyes Chicken. He started with one restaurant in New Orleans in 1972. It grew fast. Too fast. By 1990, Copeland’s empire was in deep trouble. His company, A. Copeland Enterprises, declared bankruptcy.

The banks took over Popeyes. They controlled the restaurants. They controlled the recipes. But they missed one crucial detail. Al Copeland personally owned the Popeyes brand name. He held the trademarks. The banks had the chicken, but not the name.

The banks needed that name to operate. They couldn't run Popeyes restaurants without the Popeyes name. Copeland had them. He turned their victory into his leverage. He made them pay him. To use the Popeyes name, the banks had to cut him a check.

He lost his company. But he made his creditors pay him for the very name they needed to succeed. Al Copeland turned a bankruptcy rule into a weapon. He lost everything, then he made the banks pay him for it.
